title: JavaScript Browser Environment Core Check
description: Check your understanding of the browser runtime, window, document, DOM selection and modification, events, script loading, browser APIs, storage, navigation, rendering, compatibility, and DevTools.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: What does the browser runtime provide around the JavaScript engine?

options.text: Web APIs such as `document`, `window`, `fetch`, storage, timers, and events
Only the syntax rules for functions and objects
A replacement for HTML and CSS

questions.explanation: The JavaScript engine runs the language. The browser runtime provides browser-specific APIs such as DOM, events, fetch, storage, and timers.

questions.prompt: What does `document` represent in a browser page?

options.text: The loaded HTML page as a DOM document

questions.explanation: `document` represents the loaded page and exposes the DOM APIs used to inspect and change it.

options.text: The first element that matches the CSS selector, or `null`
All matching elements as an array
A Promise for a DOM element

questions.explanation: `querySelector()` returns the first matching element in document order, or `null` if there is no match.

questions.prompt: Which method is commonly used to select all elements matching a CSS selector?
questions.explanation: `querySelectorAll()` returns a static NodeList of matching elements.

questions.prompt: Which property is usually safest for inserting plain user-provided text into an element?
questions.explanation: `textContent` treats the value as text. `innerHTML` parses strings as HTML and can be risky with untrusted content.

questions.prompt: Which API is best for adding or removing a single CSS class from an element?

options.text: Prevents the browser's default action for that event when possible
Stops JavaScript from running anywhere on the page

questions.explanation: `preventDefault()` is commonly used for forms and links when JavaScript should handle the action instead of the browser default.

options.text: Handling events from child elements with a listener on an ancestor
Running all events in a Web Worker

questions.explanation: Event delegation relies on event bubbling so a parent can handle events from matching child elements.

questions.prompt: Which script attribute downloads a classic script without blocking parsing and runs scripts in order after parsing?
questions.explanation: `defer` lets HTML parsing continue and preserves script execution order.

questions.prompt: Which statement about browser module scripts is correct?

options.text: They have module scope, support `import` and `export`, and are deferred by default
They automatically turn every top-level variable into a `window` property
They always run before the HTML parser starts

questions.explanation: Browser modules support the module system, run in their own scope, use strict mode, and are deferred by default.

questions.prompt: Which browser storage API persists string key-value data across browser restarts until cleared?
questions.explanation: `localStorage` persists for an origin until it is cleared. Values are stored as strings.

questions.prompt: What is CORS mainly about in browser JavaScript?

options.text: Whether browser JavaScript from one origin may read responses from another origin
Whether CSS selectors can match classes
Whether the DOM can contain buttons

questions.explanation: CORS is a browser security mechanism for controlled cross-origin response access.

questions.prompt: Which API is preferred for safely building query strings?
questions.explanation: `URLSearchParams` encodes query parameter names and values safely.

options.text: Checking whether an API or capability exists before using it
Guessing support from the user's screen size
Selecting all elements with a feature class

questions.explanation: Feature detection checks for support directly, such as `if ('clipboard' in navigator)`.

questions.prompt: Which DevTools panel is usually most useful for inspecting request URLs, headers, status codes, and responses?
questions.explanation: The Network panel shows browser requests and responses, including status codes, headers, payloads, and timing.
